title: Data & Insights Junior Analyst
description:
Animal Health, Planet Health - Join the Adventure at Virbac!
Initial 6-Month Contract (with view to permanent)
We're not just hiring—we're growing a movement. At Virbac, animal health is at the heart of everything we do, because we know that animal health is key to the health of the planet. When you join Virbac, you're stepping into a unique human adventure where your passion and purpose help shape a better world. Based in Australia, we're proud to develop and manufacture products that improve the wellbeing of animals—and by extension, our communities.
We're officially a 2024 Great Place to Work®! We're a specialist animal health company with a strong focus on veterinary pharmaceuticals, vaccines, pet care for dogs and cats, products for horses, cattle and sheep.
Why join us? Because at Virbac, we're Better Through People. We've got a big heart for leadership, learning, and growth—and we make it easy to love where you work. Just a few of our perks:
9 free animal health products every quarter.
Paid parental leave.
Extra leave purchase options.
Annual leave loading.
Superannuation top-ups (with salary sacrifice and company matching opportunities too).
The Opportunity
Virbac Australia has an exciting opportunity for a Data & Insights Junior Analyst to join our team on an initial 6-month contract, with a view to permanent employment. Reporting to the Data & Insights Manager, the purpose of this role is to maintain Virbac’s core data infrastructure and actively build the reporting tools the business needs to operate.
The key areas of accountability for this role are:
Data Warehouse & Pipeline Maintenance: Manage the daily operations of the SQL data warehouse and ETL pipelines. Troubleshoot and fix broken queries or data loads immediately. Ensure overnight data extracts from our ERP systems (including Movex/AS400) run successfully before the start of business.
Report Development & Power BI Operations: Oversee the daily refreshes of all Power BI dashboards. Design and build new Power BI reports and underlying datasets from scratch. Initiate the design process, build the data models, and present the first iteration for review and final sign-off by the Data & Insights Manager.
Analytical Build & Ad-Hoc Support: Act as the first point of contact for day-to-day data requests from the business. Work directly with business users to translate their vague requests into concrete analytical requirements. Build the specific measures, metrics, and DAX formulas the business needs to track performance.
System Documentation & Odyssey ERP Prep: Keep clear documentation of our data architecture, SQL queries, and reporting logic. Support data cleansing, master data mapping, and legacy system audits to prepare for the upcoming Odyssey ERP migration.
You're someone who:
Has 1 to 3 years of practical experience in database administration, SQL programming, BI reporting, and dataset design.
Holds a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Data Analytics, or an equivalent quantitative field.
Has strong hands-on experience with SQL server, relational databases, and ETL processes.
Has solid proficiency in Microsoft Power BI, including the ability to build datasets, write DAX measures, and design functional dashboards.
Has advanced Excel skills for large dataset manipulation, and the ability to extract and format data from legacy ERPs (Movex/DB2) into modern reporting tools.
Has a curious mind and loves learning new things—because growth (personal and professional) is kind of your thing.
Possesses the initiative to independently research solutions when faced with a roadblock. Relies on self-directed troubleshooting and AI-assisted iteration to solve coding problems before escalating to the Data & Insights Manager.
Shows up for your team with heart, humility, and a willingness to pitch in—no egos, just good energy.
Takes pride in doing the routine maintenance well, while also bringing initiative to the design and build of new reports.
Escalates system failures or broken refreshes immediately with a timeline for a fix, rather than waiting for end-users to notice and complain.
Not sure you tick every box? That's okay. Research shows that people from underrepresented groups often hesitate to apply unless they meet every single requirement. At Virbac, we care more about your values, your mindset, and your passion than a perfect checklist.

title: Data Scientist | Model & AI Risk
description:
Our Model Risk Management team provides independent oversight and challenge of model and AI risks are well managed across Macquarie globally. We assess whether models and AI systems are fit for purpose, appropriately controlled, and aligned to the firm’s risk appetite and to regulatory expectations. The team plays a critical role in enabling safe adoption of models and AI by providing robust validation, clear challenge and sound risk-based decisions.
At Macquarie, our advantage is bringing together diverse people and empowering them to shape all kinds of possibilities. We are a global financial services group operating in 31 markets and with 56 years of unbroken profitability. You’ll be part of a friendly and supportive team where everyone - no matter what role - contributes ideas and drives outcomes.
What role will you play?
As a Data Scientist within Model Risk Management, you will independently review, challenge and validate artificial intelligence use cases across the firm. Your work will assess whether AI systems are fit‑for‑purpose, operate as intended and ensure that the risks introduced are understood, appropriately controlled, and remain within the Macquarie’s risk appetite.
You will design and execute proportionate validation approaches, assess data, methodology, assumptions, and outcomes, and clearly articulate findings to technical and non‑technical stakeholders. Your analysis and judgement will directly inform model approvals, usage decisions, and risk acceptance.
Working closely with, but independently from, model developers, product owners, and business stakeholders, you will provide constructive challenge that enables safe and sustainable AI adoption. You will also contribute to the evolution of AI validation practices, tooling and standards within the team, sharing knowledge and strengthening collective capability.
What You Offer
A courageous mindset and a demonstrated track record of self‑directed learning, with the curiosity and discipline to stay ahead of rapidly evolving AI techniques and risks
Attention to detail and a knack for identifying problems
Experience developing or independently reviewing and validating artificial intelligence, machine learning, or statistical models
Strong programming capability in Python, R, or SQL, with experience interrogating large and complex datasets
Familiarity with modern AI techniques, including large language models, their limitations, failure modes, and associated risks
Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts and risk trade‑offs clearly to both technical and senior non‑technical stakeholders
A structured, analytical, and sceptical mindset, with the ability to form independent judgement to make sound, commercial decisions balancing risks and rewards and to prioritise work in a collaborative environment.
We love hearing from anyone inspired to build a better future with us, if you're excited about the role or working at Macquarie we encourage you to apply.

Genuinely curious and passionate about health, wellness, and fitness.

title: Lead Data Scientist - Trading
description:
Pricing is the heartbeat of wagering. Lead the data science team that sets sharper prices across sport and racing, powering real-time trading decisions that directly shape margin and customer experience. Grow a high-performing team in a collaborative, high-trust culture that values curiosity, impact and fun.
How you'll be a part of the action 
Reporting to the Head of Wagering Data Analytics and Segmentation, you will lead the design, delivery and continuous improvement of pricing and risk models that drive performance across our Wagering Trading team. You will partner with traders, product and technology to turn ideas into measurable commercial results.
Lead development of probabilistic pricing models for sport and racing markets — from fixed-odds and exotic pricing to in-play and derivative markets.
Design and improve models that generate accurate and competitive prices across thoroughbred, harness, greyhound and multi-sport events.
Build models that account for market dynamics, form, conditions, venue and real-time signals to produce prices that balance competitiveness with margin.
Partner with traders to develop automated pricing and risk frameworks that reduce manual intervention and improve speed to market.
Create model monitoring and feedback loops — tracking price accuracy, overrounds, market movement and settlement outcomes to continuously improve model performance.
Shape and grow a high-performing data science team with clear standards, strong coaching and a focus on delivery.
Champion ethical, purpose-led use of data to enhance customer outcomes and meet regulatory obligations.
What you'll need to succeed
You are a curious, hands-on leader who balances scientific rigour with practical delivery. You understand how a wagering trading operation works and know what good pricing looks like — not just mathematically, but commercially.
Deep experience in wagering, sports betting or racing pricing — you understand how odds are formed, how markets move, and where model-driven pricing creates edge.
Proven track record building probabilistic models for event outcomes — win/place, head-to-head, line, total, multi-leg and in-play markets.
Experience working with racing form data, ratings, speed maps, track/weather conditions and translating these into pricing inputs.
Understanding of overround management, liability and risk exposure and how pricing models interact with trading decisions.
Familiarity with real-time data feeds and low-latency environments — pricing models that need to perform under event-time pressure, not just in batch.
Proven ability to lead, coach and grow data scientists and modellers.
Strong programming capability in Python and SQL, with experience in modern ML frameworks and cloud platforms (Databricks, AWS, MLflow or similar).
Ability to translate complex analysis into clear stories and decisions for traders, product teams and senior leaders.
Proven capability to design model governance, documentation and testing disciplines.
What will set you apart
Experience with Australian racing and/or sport wagering markets specifically.
Background in Bayesian modelling, simulation or stochastic methods applied to pricing.
Exposure to reinforcement learning or dynamic pricing optimisation for in-play or live markets.
Understanding of customer-level pricing dynamics — how price sensitivity, segmentation and market positioning interact with margin targets.
Experience operating within a licensed, regulated wagering environment and understanding of responsible gambling obligations.

We know that when we belong, we thrive. That’s why we offer:
Time for moments that matter - from birthdays to cultural leave, flexible public holidays, and 5 days bonus leave
18 weeks paid parental leave for every new parent, no matter your role

Establish data governance practices including cataloguing, lineage, access controls and compliance frameworks

Experience with modern data tooling such as dbt, Airflow, Dagster, Spark, Snowflake, BigQuery or Redshift

title: Staff ML Engineer
description:
About Buildkite
Buildkite's CI platform is trusted by the world's leading engineering teams, shipping software to over 1,000,000,000 daily users.
Job Overview
We're hiring a Staff Engineer (ML) to join our Test Engine team. In this role, you'll define and lead the technical strategy for machine learning within Test Engine — specifically, building the models and infrastructure behind predictive test selection: using code changes to determine which tests actually need to run.
Staff Engineers at Buildkite are hands-on technical leaders. You'll influence how we design, build, and scale systems while supporting other engineers to deliver their best work. You'll be the most senior ML practitioner in the company, setting the technical direction for how we approach test selection and establishing the patterns and infrastructure that the broader ML effort builds on.
🔧 About the Team
The Test Engine team helps engineering teams ship faster by giving them visibility and control over their test suites. Today, that means real-time flaky test detection and management, intelligent test splitting across parallel jobs, and performance analytics and tracing — all working across any CI/CD platform, not just Buildkite Pipelines.
Test Engine already ingests billions of test runs. We have deep visibility into test suites, codebases, and the relationships between them. The next step is using that data to answer a fundamental question: for a given code change, which tests are most likely to fail?
We believe the industry is moving away from running full test suites on every change. The teams that can shift their outer testing loop into a fast, precise inner loop — running only the tests that matter — will ship value to their customers dramatically faster. For many of our customers, that speed is existential. Switching costs are low, competition is fierce, and the teams with faster feedback loops win.
This is where ML comes in. If we can model the relationship between code changes and test failures, we can give engineering teams a fundamentally faster development cycle. We're not trying to optimise individual tests — we're trying to build a generalised solution to test selection that works across codebases, frameworks, and languages.
🚀 What You'll Do
Own Technical Direction for ML in Test Engine
Lead and define the ML strategy for predictive test selection — from early experimentation through to models running reliably in production at scale

title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer - Integrations & Solutions Group (AU remote)
description:
Company Description
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.
Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora,你好, hallo, vítejte!
Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time consuming and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point. 
Where and how you can work
Our flagship campus is in Sydney, with a second campus in Melbourne and co-working spaces in Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide, and Auckland, NZ. You have flexibility in how and where you work — whether that's from one of our spaces, from home, or a mix of both. This role is remote-friendly within Australia, so you can choose the setup that empowers you and your team to do your best work.
Job Description
About the team
We aim to build the world’s richest Ecosystem of apps for visual design and communications that supercharge Canva’s ability to meet the diverse needs of a billion users and drive Canva’s MAU growth.
With the proliferation of innovations in generative AI and as large organizations have increasingly complex workflows to manage their designs, Canva is well poised to become the platform that simplifies access and discovery of services related to visual design. We are already working with hundreds of developers to enable access to these exciting products with our Apps SDK and Canva public REST API!
As one of the groups in Ecosystem, the Integrations and Solutions Group builds Canva's AI integration layer — the infrastructure that connects Canva's design capabilities to the world's leading AI assistants. Our teams own the MCP platform, AI-optimised tools and APIs, evaluation frameworks, and the agent architecture that powers millions of AI-driven design interactions. We work directly with partners like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, and we're in the middle of a strategic shift from protocol-first integrations toward intelligent, Canva-hosted design agents.
As a Staff Machine Learning Engineer, you'll play a critical role in defining how AI platforms experience Canva — driving the technical standards, evaluation frameworks, and architectural decisions that ensure our integrations are reliable, measurable, and evolving with a rapidly changing ecosystem.
What you’d be doing in this role
As Canva scales change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.
At the moment, this role is focused on:
Drive the design and evolution of AI-ready tools and APIs that enable LLM platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and others) to reliably interact with Canva's design capabilities — defining the patterns and standards that other teams adopt for tool descriptions, payload structures, and intent-based interfaces. Pioneer agent-to-agent communication approaches.
Own and evolve evaluation frameworks that systematically measure tool-use accuracy across platforms — defining what "good" looks like for proxy-based fast evals and real-client production evals, and ensuring these frameworks scale as we add platforms and capabilities.
Shape Canva's agent architecture — making strategic technical decisions about where intelligence should live (in external LLMs vs Canva-hosted agents), building the orchestration layers that allow third-party providers to invoke Canva's design tools at scale, and driving automation of complex workflows like marketing campaigns.
Define and build observability systems that give multiple teams visibility into how AI assistants consume Canva's tools in production — identifying failure patterns, setting quality benchmarks, and closing the loop between production data and continuous improvement.
Work across team and platform boundaries — proactively identifying problems not yet defined, understanding behavioural quirks across LLM platforms, and driving solutions that span the AI Integrations, API Capabilities, and Workflow Integrations teams.
Influence integration strategy with AI partners and internal teams — contributing to technical direction with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, and shaping how Canva's broader engineering organisation builds for AI consumption.
You're probably a match if
You've shipped LLM-powered systems into production and can quantify your impact — things like improving tool-call accuracy from X% to Y%, reducing agent error rates, cutting latency by Z%, or measurably improving user outcomes through better AI integration. We care about results, not just launches.
You proactively find and solve problems others haven't defined yet — you've identified gaps in how LLMs consume tools or APIs, scoped the problem across teams, and driven the fix without waiting for someone to hand you a brief.
You've built or owned evaluation pipelines end-to-end — designing metrics, building benchmarking infrastructure, and using data to make architectural decisions about AI integrations at scale.
You set technical standards that others follow — whether that's tool design patterns, API contracts for AI agents, documentation quality, or observability practices. Your work becomes the reference point.
You can connect external ecosystem changes to internal strategy — when a new LLM capability drops or a partner shifts their architecture, you can quickly assess the implications for Canva and re-prioritise accordingly.
You're proficient in Python and familiar with ML frameworks, and equally comfortable working with TypeScript/Node.js and cloud infrastructure (Cloudflare Workers, AWS, or similar).
You thrive in cross-team, partner-facing work — influencing engineering, product, and external AI platform teams to shape integration strategy. You're comfortable operating across team boundaries without formal authority.
You're energised by ambiguity and pace — the AI ecosystem is evolving rapidly, and you bring clarity and momentum rather than waiting for direction.
Additional Information
Don't tick all the boxes? Don't worry about that - nobody does!  
We’d still love to hear from you! At Canva, we know that great engineers come from a variety of backgrounds, and we value passion, curiosity, and a willingness to learn just as much as specific experience. If you're excited about this role but don’t tick every box, we encourage you to apply, you might a great fit in ways you didn’t expect!
What's in it for you?
Achieving our crazy big goals motivates us to work hard - and we do - but you'll experience lots of moments of magic, connectivity and fun woven throughout life at Canva, too. We also offer a stack of benefits to set you up for every success in and outside of work.
Here's a taste of what's on offer:
Equity packages - we want our success to be yours too
Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more
Flexible leave options that empower you to be a force for good, take time to recharge and supports you personally
